segmentChecks.note: Given/when/then preserve universal in-scope coverage, the >10 trigger, and the required <=10 result; why preserves the testability rationale.
Why accurately retains complexity as an approximation of the test cases needed to pin behaviour.
Why retains the approximate ten-path point, loss of full coverage, and defects settling in untested paths.
Why preserves the responsibility-level sensor interpretation and warns that hiding branching merely hides the signal.
The preference for coherent named responsibilities, prohibitions on relocation and opaque encoding, and evidence requirement preserve nameability, testability, and reasoning.
Prefer[0] explicitly says to diagnose first and group decisions by policy or responsibility before extraction.
Prefer[0] preserves grouping branches by the policy or responsibility they implement.
Prefer[0] preserves distinguishing validation and guards from the core operation; 'separate' is a reasonable imperative compression in this diagnostic checklist.
Prefer[0] retains identification of repeated compound conditions that form a domain predicate.
Prefer[3] preserves both dispatch table and strategy and restricts them to a genuinely stable key-to-behaviour mapping.
Prefer[4] preserves the requirement that caller control flow reveal the important choices.
Avoid[1] retains indirect structures and opaque encodings used solely to lower the score; prefer[4] retains the associated caller-readability safeguard.
Avoid[2] preserves scattering one policy across tiny functions and the harder-to-follow interaction as the reason not to do so.
The evidence array performs the source Verify heading's structural role and contains its checks.

The shared strict-disposition node explicitly preserves failure on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline, and applicability to unchanged code; verifier_detail and audit also retain strict.
When and verifier_detail reproduce every decision-point category, including else if, do, case, all three operators, and ternaries.
The base of 1 and each additive decision keyword, boolean/nullish operator, and ternary are preserved exactly.
Prefer[1] retains extraction of a coherent decision or policy into an intention-revealing function.
Avoid[3] explicitly protects boolean semantics, branch order, and fallback behaviour, reinforced by then's no-behaviour-change requirement.
Evidence[2] requires extracted code to introduce no new nesting, duplication, or length violation.
Unless, activation, and verifier_detail consistently exclude test files and vendored/build directories from the scan.

risks: The term 'code lines' is not defined, so blank lines, comments, and multiline expressions could make the under-three-line exemption inconsistent.
The coder-facing fields do not explicitly instruct the coder to rerun the detector and behaviour/path-focused tests after refactoring; those verification steps are carried in evidence instead.

review.summary: All shared and auditor-compressed segments retain their decision-relevant knowledge at the claimed destinations, and the additional spot checks also pass. The counting rule, scope, exclusions, strict handling of unchanged findings, and refactoring safeguards are clear enough for implementation; only the inherited ambiguity in 'code lines' and separation of verification into evidence remain minor risks. I agree with the auditor's PASS verdict.
